title: How a reconnecting stream replays events

plan.subject: area
rationale: Recorded runs of the reconnect driver show what the browser receives for each drop.
The producer recording adds a second dataset because it shows task switching that the stream runs cannot show.
The terms dataset is authored because names are read from the code and no run shows them.

scope.summary: The event log and read() in src/stream.py, and the producer in src/producer.py.

sections.title: The names in the stream
sections.body: Four names carry this lesson. Two belong to reading and two to the paths a read takes.

checkpoints.prompt: Which name is raised when the cursor is past the last event?

options.why: That one marks a cursor exactly at the end.
read() raises it when the cursor is past the end.
That is a path that yields events.

checkpoints.explanation: The first check in read() compares the cursor with the end.

sections.title: One reconnect, shown whole
sections.body: The browser drops after frame 2 and reconnects with Last-Event-ID 2. Compare what the transcript has with what the browser received.

notes.text: The browser gets the thinking event as frame 4.

elements.caption: read(), a few lines at a time

steps.note: A cursor past the end raises Beyond.
A running turn follows. A finished one replays.
Replay yields each stored event after the cursor.

checkpoints.prompt: Five events are stored and the cursor is 2. Which frames does replay yield?

options.why: The frame number is the index plus one.
That is what the old reader sends.
Replay starts at the index equal to the cursor.

checkpoints.explanation: Index 2 holds the third event, sent as frame 3.

checkpoints.prompt: Click the prompts the browser received.

sections.title: When the cursor runs ahead
sections.body: Now the browser drops after frame 2 but sends Last-Event-ID 4. The old reader ignores the cursor. The new one trusts it.

elements.caption: What does the new reader lose?
What kind is each stored event?

checkpoints.prompt: The new reader resumes from cursor 4. Click the frames the browser never gets.
checkpoints.explanation: Frames 3 and 4 sit between the drop and the cursor.

checkpoints.prompt: Fill in the kind of frames 3 to 5.
checkpoints.explanation: The second turn is a prompt, a thinking event and an answer.

sections.title: Try every reconnect
sections.body: Move the drop and the cursor. Watch which branch of read() runs for each case.

checkpoints.prompt: The turn is running and the cursor is 4 with 3 events stored. Which branch runs?

options.why: The running check comes after the Beyond check.
The cursor is past the end, so the first check fires.
Replay runs only for a finished turn.

checkpoints.explanation: The Beyond check runs before the running check.

sections.body: Predict the branches one run takes. Then step through two producer tasks that share the event loop.

elements.caption: How do tasks A and B take turns?

checkpoints.prompt: The browser reconnects with cursor 4 while turn 2 runs. Click the nodes this run reaches.
checkpoints.explanation: Three events are stored, so cursor 4 is past the end.

checkpoints.prompt: Task A has appended its first item. What does `items` hold now?

options.why: The two tasks do not share a list.
Each task appends to its own list.

checkpoints.explanation: Each call of produce() gets a new empty list.

final.prompt: The browser drops after frame 3 and sends Last-Event-ID 4. Click the frames it never gets.
final.explanation: Only frame 4 sits between the drop and the cursor.

view.caption: A copy of one recorded reconnect

final.explanation: Frame 3 carries event id 4, but replay sends each event under its own id.

final.prompt: The turn is running. Fill in the kind of each stored event.
final.explanation: Turn 1 is a prompt and an answer, and turn 2 has only its prompt so far.

final.prompt: Why does the old reader send frames 1 and 2 twice after a reconnect?

options.text: The browser asks for them again.
options.why: The browser sends a cursor, which read_old drops.
The transcript lane shows each event once.

final.explanation: read_old calls replay with 0 in place of the cursor.
